summary:
FIELD SHIFT is a NASA Earth observation-powered agricultural decision-support platform designed to help farmers adapt to changing climate conditions and water scarcity. Integrating real-time and historical NASA POWER data, the platform transforms meteorological observations into actionable agroclimatic insights using FAO-56 Penman–Monteith evapotranspiration modelling.

It combines crop water requirement estimation, soil moisture and root-zone water balance analysis, crop rotation planning, and irrigation strategy simulation. Farmers can configure their farm profiles, evaluate different adaptation scenarios, compare rainfed and irrigation-based approaches, and generate evidence-backed reports to support agricultural decisions.

By connecting satellite-derived Earth observations with scientifically grounded agricultural models, FIELD SHIFT bridges the gap between complex climate data and practical farm management. It aims to promote more informed water use, strengthen agricultural resilience, and help farming communities make better adaptation decisions in an increasingly uncertain climate.
details:
FIELD SHIFT

FIELD SHIFT is an integrated agricultural intelligence and climate adaptation platform that transforms NASA Earth observation data into practical, science-based farming decisions. It bridges the gap between satellite-derived environmental information and on-ground agricultural management by combining NASA POWER meteorological observations with established FAO-56 agricultural models.

How It Works?

The platform allows users to configure farm profiles, including geographical coordinates, soil hydraulic properties, crops, irrigation infrastructure, and cultivation history. It retrieves daily meteorological observations from NASA POWER, including temperature, precipitation, relative humidity, wind speed, and solar radiation.

Using the FAO-56 Penman–Monteith method, FIELD SHIFT calculates reference evapotranspiration (ET₀), which is subsequently combined with crop coefficients (Kc) to estimate crop evapotranspiration (ETc). Its soil-water intelligence engine models root-zone water depletion, total available water (TAW), readily available water (RAW), and crop water stress using the FAO-56 water-balance methodology.

Beyond monitoring conditions, the Adaptation Studio enables users to compare rainfed, supplemental irrigation, and full-irrigation strategies. It evaluates irrigation demand, application efficiency, delivery-capacity constraints, water stress, and soil-water dynamics. The crop rotation module additionally evaluates crop sequences and relevant pathogen-history constraints. Users can generate comprehensive reports containing scenario comparisons, scientific calculations, visual evidence, and data provenance.

Technology and Tools:

The platform is developed using Next.js, React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS, with Python-independent, server-side TypeScript calculation engines and validated API contracts using Zod. NASA POWER provides the Earth observation data, while Vitest, ESLint, and TypeScript support testing and quality assurance. The application uses responsive dashboards, interactive charts, browser-based report printing, and JSON/Markdown exports.

Innovation and Creativity:

FIELD SHIFT goes beyond displaying satellite observations. Its central innovation is connecting Earth intelligence with a deterministic agricultural decision-support workflow. Instead of presenting isolated weather statistics, it translates environmental conditions into crop water requirements, soil-water stress indicators, irrigation comparisons, and adaptation insights. It also explicitly handles missing observations without silently replacing unavailable measurements with fabricated values.

Intended Impact:

The project aims to help farmers, agricultural researchers, and extension professionals make more informed decisions about irrigation, crop selection, and climate adaptation. By improving the accessibility and interpretation of Earth observation data, FIELD SHIFT supports more responsible water management, strengthens agricultural resilience, and contributes towards more sustainable farming practices under increasing climate uncertainty.
